<!-- HOVER TOOLKIT — body-level tooltip card + affordance styles. Keep this block;
     it is inert until an element carries data-tip. Usage:
       term:      <span class="term" data-tiphead="Flow matching" data-tip="Plain-language explanation.">flow matching</span>
       forensics: <span class="finfo" data-tiphead="Figure forensics" data-tip="No error bars; log axis compresses divergence.">ⓘ forensics</span>
       SVG box:   <g data-tiphead="Codec encoder" data-tip="What this component does.">…</g>
       figure overlay: transparent absolutely-positioned <span data-tip=…> over an <img> region.
     Rules: no double quotes inside data-tip values; the card must stay appended to
     document.body — reveal.js scales the slide container with a CSS transform, where
     position:fixed and CSS-only popovers break. -->
<style>
.term { border-bottom: 1px dashed #3d5a8c; cursor: help; }
.finfo { display: inline-block; margin-left: 12px; padding: 1px 12px 2px; border: 1px solid #1e3a66; border-radius: 999px; color: #3b82f6; font-size: 0.42em; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.06em; vertical-align: middle; cursor: help; }
.finfo:hover { border-color: #3b82f6; background: rgba(59,130,246,0.08); }
</style>
<script>
(function () {
  if (document.getElementById('tipcard')) return;
  const css = document.createElement('style');
  css.textContent = `
    #tipcard { position: fixed; display: none; max-width: 460px; background: #0a0e17; border: 1px solid #2a2a2a; border-left: 3px solid #3b82f6; border-radius: 10px; padding: 12px 16px; z-index: 9999; box-shadow: 0 10px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.65); pointer-events: none; font-family: 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; }
    #tipcard .tip-head { color: #3b82f6; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.09em; text-transform: uppercase; margin-bottom: 5px; }
    #tipcard .tip-body { color: #d6d9dc; font-size: 15px; line-height: 1.5; font-weight: 400; }
    body.tips-off #tipcard { display: none !important; }
    body.tips-off [data-tip] { border-bottom-color: transparent !important; text-decoration: none !important; cursor: default !important; }
    #tip-toggle { position: fixed; top: 12px; left: 56px; z-index: 9999; font: 600 12px/1 system-ui, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.05em; padding: 7px 14px; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid #2a2a2a; background: rgba(17,17,17,0.92); color: #3b82f6; cursor: pointer; opacity: 0.3; transition: opacity 0.15s ease; }
    #tip-toggle:hover { opacity: 1; }
    #tip-toggle.tips-off { text-decoration: line-through; }
    @media print { #tip-toggle { display: none !important; } }`;
  document.head.appendChild(css);
  const card = document.createElement('div');
  card.id = 'tipcard';
  card.innerHTML = '<div class="tip-head"></div><div class="tip-body"></div>';
  document.body.appendChild(card);
  const btn = document.createElement('button');
  btn.id = 'tip-toggle'; btn.type = 'button'; btn.textContent = 'Tips';
  btn.title = 'Hover tooltips are on — click to disable';
  btn.addEventListener('click', () => {
    const off = document.body.classList.toggle('tips-off');
    btn.classList.toggle('tips-off', off);
    btn.textContent = off ? 'Tips off' : 'Tips';
    btn.title = off ? 'Hover tooltips are off — click to enable' : 'Hover tooltips are on — click to disable';
  });
  document.body.appendChild(btn);
  const head = card.firstChild, body = card.lastChild;
  const place = (ev) => {
    const pad = 16, r = card.getBoundingClientRect();
    let x = ev.clientX + pad, y = ev.clientY + pad;
    if (x + r.width > innerWidth - 10) x = ev.clientX - r.width - pad;
    if (y + r.height > innerHeight - 10) y = ev.clientY - r.height - pad;
    card.style.left = Math.max(8, x) + 'px'; card.style.top = Math.max(8, y) + 'px';
  };
  document.addEventListener('mousemove', (ev) => {
    const t = ev.target.closest && ev.target.closest('[data-tip]');
    if (t) {
      head.textContent = t.getAttribute('data-tiphead') || 'Explanation';
      body.textContent = t.getAttribute('data-tip');
      card.style.display = 'block';
      place(ev);
    } else {
      card.style.display = 'none';
    }
  });
})();
</script>

# **Forge**

## Fast builds by default: parse once, cache the work, ship the artifacts

<p class="byline">A guided code tour for people who need the mental model before the details</p>

<p class="links"><a href="https://your.gitlab/org/repo">your.gitlab/org/repo</a></p>

<a class="slide-id" id="ea58ee63-d173-4e06-860a-815b83391e55"></a>

<!-- _class: lead -->

## What this deck gives you

**Forge** is a cache-aware build engine. This tour gives you a mental model of the **CLI -> Engine -> Store** pipeline, then points you at the files and tests that prove the model.

Every diagram box and file name is a **clickable link** into [`your.gitlab/org/repo`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo), pinned to commit `COMMIT` so you can verify each claim as you go.

# The Big **Picture**

---

<a class="slide-id" id="8c226908-49d4-43ea-9c08-a28383e720d7"></a>

## Forge turns rebuilds into change decisions

> **Forge** parses a project into a typed program, runs only the work that changed, and persists artifacts so the next build can skip repeated work.

<div class="columns">
<div>

### The shape

- **CLI** accepts user intent and config
- **Engine** evaluates the typed build plan
- **Store** owns cache reads, writes, and artifacts

</div>
<div>

### The payoff

- No daemon required for incremental builds
- Pure core logic stays easy to test
- <span class="tag tag-accent">Warm cache</span> should feel almost idle

</div>
</div>

---

<a class="slide-id" id="724281b4-72f7-4fb3-8cff-508514cfc57c"></a>

## The architecture is three boundaries, not three folders

The CLI turns text into intent, the Engine makes deterministic decisions, and the Store isolates all filesystem/cache behavior.

<!--FIG:arch-hero-->

<span class="tag tag-blue">Tap any box</span> CLI -> [`cli.py`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo/-/blob/COMMIT/src/cli.py) · Parser -> [`parser.py`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo/-/blob/COMMIT/src/parser.py) · Engine -> [`engine.py`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo/-/blob/COMMIT/src/engine.py) · Store -> [`store.py`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo/-/blob/COMMIT/src/infra/store.py)

# Run **It**

---

<a class="slide-id" id="6724a7b7-88b4-4ade-aeee-105e48ce83e4"></a>

## Run twice: the second build should mostly disappear

```bash
git clone https://your.gitlab/org/repo && cd repo
pip install -e .

forge run ./examples/hello     # cold cache: parse, compute, store
forge run ./examples/hello     # warm cache: reuse stored artifacts
```

<div class="columns">
<div>

### What to notice

- The command path starts in [`src/cli.py`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo/-/blob/COMMIT/src/cli.py)
- The Engine receives a typed plan, not raw files
- Cache hits should bypass compute work

</div>
<div>

### What to open next

- [`examples/hello`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo/-/tree/COMMIT/examples/hello)
- [`tests/test_cache.py`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo/-/blob/COMMIT/tests/test_cache.py)
- [`src/infra/store.py`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo/-/blob/COMMIT/src/infra/store.py)

</div>
</div>

<a class="slide-id" id="5a9937cf-c1d3-4651-afd2-b1c8e5716993"></a>

# The **Layers**

---

<a class="slide-id" id="65ce97fc-31c8-4c37-96b0-d14002e7252b"></a>

## The dependency rule keeps the domain small

Each layer only depends on the one below it. The Domain is pure, so most behavior can be tested without touching the filesystem.

<!--FIG:layers-->

---

<a class="slide-id" id="8d3587b9-0dfc-4ff9-8a27-99a5235888a4"></a>

<!-- _class: invert -->

# A Request, **End to End**

---

<a class="slide-id" id="93fbf818-3fca-4f64-b5f5-01adbe2355a3"></a>

## The Store boundary is the hot path

The Engine never reaches into the filesystem directly. Cache lookup, compute-on-miss, and artifact writes all go through the Store.

<!--FIGSM:request-flow-->

---

<a class="slide-id" id="089b706b-8ed9-4903-9a19-eada51ae155a"></a>

## Key terms

<div class="columns">
<div class="card">

### AST
The typed tree the **Parser** produces from raw source; the Engine never sees loose text.

### Step
One cacheable unit of work in the Engine.

</div>
<div class="card">

### Cache key
A content hash of a step's inputs. Same key means the artifact can be reused.

### Artifact
A persisted output owned by the **Store** and keyed for later reuse.

</div>
</div>

<a class="slide-id" id="205cdba8-153d-4d33-a16a-cfbb14bdf746"></a>

<!-- _class: invert -->

# Design **Guardrails**

---

<a class="slide-id" id="d23c5a99-28ce-4963-b828-f9196598b944"></a>

## The design rules keep reviews fast

<div class="columns">
<div>

- **Pure core, I/O at the edges** — Domain code never imports `os`
- **Types are the spec** — `mypy --strict` catches interface drift
- **Every bug gets a test first** — reproduce, then patch

</div>
<div>

- **Small PRs, fast review** — <span class="tag tag-accent">&lt; 400 lines</span> is the norm
- **Interfaces over implementations** — one Store protocol, many backends
- **Docs live next to code** — stale docs are treated as bugs

</div>
</div>

## Where to look

| Add a CLI flag | [`src/cli.py`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo/-/blob/COMMIT/src/cli.py) |
| Change how input is parsed | [`src/parser.py`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo/-/blob/COMMIT/src/parser.py) |
| Add a build step | [`src/domain/`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo/-/tree/COMMIT/src/domain) + [`tests/test_engine.py`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo/-/blob/COMMIT/tests/test_engine.py) |
| Add a cache backend | [`src/infra/store.py`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo/-/blob/COMMIT/src/infra/store.py) |
| Understand a failing build | [`src/observability/`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo/-/tree/COMMIT/src/observability) + [`tests/test_logging.py`](https://your.gitlab/org/repo/-/blob/COMMIT/tests/test_logging.py) |
